title: DeliverySyncRequest
description: Body of `PUT /delivery/v1/operations/{operationKey}`: Factory asks the `youtrack` service to perform ONE issue write (delivery link, comment, non-resolving transition, or owner-accepted resolve). The service is the only holder of the vendor credential and performs the write itself (D113 clause 1). Idempotency and recovery semantics are in `docs/task-delivery.md` §Recovery; in short: the same `operationKey` with the same canonical body replays the stored operation, the same key with a different body is `operation_key_conflict`, and an uncertain vendor outcome is settled by read-back over a quiet window, never by blind resend. Retention matters to recovery (v0.35.0): a lookup miss for a key older than the service's coverage floor does not prove the key was never used, so `reservedAt` is carried here to let the service refuse a write it cannot prove is fresh. See `docs/task-delivery.md` §Retention coverage.

operationKey.description: Minted by Factory and persisted in Factory's own store (reserved) BEFORE the first send, so a Factory restart can look the operation up instead of minting a new one. MUST equal the `{operationKey}` path segment. Recommended form: `<deliveryId>:<kind>:<stage-or-purpose>:<n>`.

reservedAt.description: When Factory minted this key. Optional, but Factory SHOULD send it on every request and MUST persist it verbatim with the rest of the body (it is part of the hashed canonical body, so a replay must repeat it exactly). It is the only way the service can apply the coverage gate on the WRITE path: if it is earlier than the service's `coveredSince` (see `delivery.operation-coverage`), the service MUST refuse with `operation_lookup_out_of_coverage` and write nothing, because it cannot prove this key was never already used — the record may have been stored, completed and purged. `null` or absent means the caller asserts the key is fresh; the service then accepts it as a new reservation but the lookup path is correspondingly weaker for it. See `docs/task-delivery.md` §Retention coverage.

expectedScope.description: The `scope.fingerprint` Factory's authorization was granted against. The service re-reads the issue and rejects with `scope_changed` (no write) on mismatch. May be `null` only for `link` and `comment` (so Factory can still post e.g. 'scope changed, re-approval required'); REQUIRED non-null for `transition` and `resolve`.

expectedState.description: Optional precondition: the state name Factory last observed. Mismatch is rejected `state_changed` (no write). `null` = no state precondition.

planHash.description: The approved plan/scope hash this write belongs to.

candidateRevision.description: Full 40-hex commit SHA of the candidate this write concerns; `null` before a candidate exists.

stage.description: Factory stage name this write reports (e.g. `planned`, `implementing`, `ready-for-testing`, `accepted`). Free text over Factory's own stage list.

linkPayload.title: DeliveryLinkPayload
linkPayload.description: Attach Factory's delivery link to the issue. Representation on the vendor side (a marked comment or an existing URL field) is the service's choice, but it MUST be identifiable on read-back and surface in `delivery.issue.deliveryLinks`.

text.description: Markdown. The service appends an invisible or trailing marker carrying `operationKey` so read-back can find exactly this comment.

targetState.description: An existing state name from `delivery.workflow` whose `resolved` is false. A resolved target is rejected `acceptance_required`: only `resolve` can resolve.
An existing state whose `resolved` is true.

acceptanceRef.title: DeliveryAcceptanceRef
acceptanceRef.description: Reference to the owner's explicit acceptance, a `delivery.decision` of kind `owner-acceptance`. The schema makes it structurally impossible to send a policy authorization, a ready-for-test state, a machine verification, a worker exit or a coordinator approval here, but a schema alone does NOT authenticate an owner: the service must also enforce the checks listed in `docs/task-delivery.md` §Resolve enforcement.

deploymentId.description: The exact dev deployment the owner tested.
